subject: Logic
title: Arrow's Voting Impossibility
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Arrow's Voting Impossibility.

hook.text: Can a voting system perfectly represent every voter's preferences? Kenneth Arrow won a Nobel for proving it can't.

buildup.text: Arrow required fairness conditions: no dictator, independence of irrelevant alternatives, and Pareto efficiency.

discovery.text: He proved no ranked voting system with three or more options can satisfy all conditions simultaneously.

twist.text: This doesn't mean democracy is useless—it means every voting system involves tradeoffs between fairness criteria.

climax.text: The proof shifted political science from searching for the perfect system to understanding unavoidable compromises.

punchline.text: Fairness for all is a proven impossibility.

quiz.question: What did Arrow's theorem prove?
options: No ranked voting system satisfies all fairness conditions
